verses.text: In the same way, wives, submit to your own husbands, so that if any of them don’t believe the word, they may be won over without words by the way you live,
when they see your pure and respectful conduct.
Your beauty shouldn’t come from outward things like elaborate hairstyles, gold jewelry, or fine clothes.
Instead, let it come from your inner self: the lasting beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is precious to God.
That’s how the holy women of the past who put their hope in God made themselves beautiful. They submitted to their own husbands,
like Sarah, who obeyed Abraham and called him her lord. You are her daughters if you do what is right and don’t give in to fear.
In the same way, husbands, live with your wives thoughtfully and honor them as the more delicate partner and as fellow heirs of the gift of life, so that nothing will block your prayers.
Finally, all of you, be united in purpose, sympathetic, loving as family, tenderhearted, and humble.
Don’t repay evil with evil or insult with insult. Instead, repay them with blessing, because you were called to inherit a blessing.
“For whoever wants to love life and see good days must keep their tongue from evil and their lips from deceitful speech.
They must turn from evil and do good; they must seek peace and pursue it.
For the Lord’s eyes are on the righteous, and his ears are open to their prayer. But the Lord opposes those who do evil.”
Who can harm you if you’re eager to do what’s good?
But even if you suffer for doing what’s right, you’re blessed. Don’t be afraid of their threats or intimidated.
Instead, honor Christ as Lord in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to anyone who asks why you have this hope. Do it with gentleness and respect,
keeping a clear conscience, so that those who insult your good behavior in Christ will be ashamed of their slander.
It’s better, if it’s God’s will, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil.
Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the spirit.
In the spirit he also went and made a proclamation to the spirits in prison,
who disobeyed long ago when God patiently waited in Noah’s days while the ark was being built. In it, a few people—eight altogether—were saved through water.
That water symbolizes baptism, which now saves you—not as a removal of dirt from the body, but as a pledge to God from a good conscience. It saves you through Jesus Christ’s resurrection,
who has gone into heaven and is at God’s right hand, with angels, authorities, and powers under his rule.
